source.title: Channel 4 makes TV history with Britain’s first AI presenter
source.credit_display_rule: at least 42px at 1080px output width for full asset duration

claim_bindings.spoken_claim_text: The programme's own presenter appeared throughout reporting from different locations and was entirely AI-generated.
required_source_phrases: programme's own presenter
appears throughout reporting from different locations
entirely AI-generated

claim_bindings.spoken_claim_text: The programme was Will AI Take My Job?
required_source_phrases: Will AI Take My Job?
Dispatches investigates how AI automation is reshaping the workplace

claim_bindings.spoken_claim_text: The presenter's face, voice and movements were made with AI, without a single frame of real-world filming.
required_source_phrases: their face, voice and movements all created through AI technology
without a single frame of real-world filming

claim_bindings.spoken_claim_text: The presenter said: Some of you might have guessed: I don't exist, I wasn't on location reporting this story.
required_source_phrases: Some of you might have guessed: I don't exist, I wasn't on location reporting this story.

claim_bindings.spoken_claim_text: The presenter said: Because I'm not real.
required_source_phrases: Because I'm not real.

claim_bindings.spoken_claim_text: Channel 4 did it on purpose as a deliberate stunt.
required_source_phrases: as part of a deliberate on-screen stunt to show just how convincing artificial intelligence has become

claim_bindings.spoken_claim_text: Louisa Compton said it showed how easy it is to hoodwink audiences with content they cannot verify.
required_source_phrases: how easy it is to hoodwink audiences with content they have no way of verifying

claim_bindings.spoken_claim_text: Louisa Compton was Channel 4's head of news.
required_source_phrases: Louisa Compton, Head of News and Current Affairs, Specialist Factual and Sport at Channel 4, said:
